name: ScrollSnap
src_typeComment: Drop on the same GameObject as a ScrollRect whose Content uses a Horizontal or Vertical Layout Group with evenly-sized items. Dragging, flinging and the elastic bounce all behave exactly as a plain ScrollRect does; the snap waits until the motion has SETTLED and then eases the nearest item to centre.  HOW IT WORKS, because the maths is the whole tool:  1. A ScrollRect does not expose "which item am I on". It exposes normalizedPosition, a 0..1 value describing how far along the SCROLLABLE RANGE you are — and the scrollable range is (content size - viewport size), NOT the content size. An item's index therefore has no direct relationship to a normalized position, which is where most snap implementations go wrong. 2. To CENTRE item i: take that item's centre measured from the content's leading edge, subtract half a viewport (that is what moves it from the leading edge to the middle), and divide by the scrollable range. See ComputeCenteredNormalizedPosition. 3. To find which item you are ON: express the VIEWPORT's centre in the content's coordinates and pick the item whose centre is nearest it. See GetNearestItemIndex.  WHO OWNS THE MOTION, which is the other half of the tool:  Dragging   the ScrollRect. We only watch. Settling   STILL the ScrollRect — its inertia, deceleration and elastic bounce run untouched. We wait. Snapping   us. The ScrollRect's velocity is zeroed every frame so only one system writes the position.  The previous version snapped from the instant you let go, which is exactly when inertia should be starting — so the fling was overwritten before it could travel, and because nothing zeroed the ScrollRect's velocity the two systems wrote the position on the same frames and fought.

src_serialized.name: horizontal
src_serialized.tooltip: If true, snaps along the horizontal axis; otherwise vertical.

src_serialized.name: snapSpeed
src_serialized.tooltip: How quickly the scroll eases into the snapped position once the snap has taken over.

src_serialized.name: snapWhenSlowerThan
src_serialized.tooltip: The scroll keeps its own momentum until it slows below this many units per second, then the snap takes over. LOWER = the scroll glides longer and the snap is a barely-visible final correction. HIGHER = the snap grabs control earlier and feels more decisive.

src_serialized.name: inputQuietTime
src_serialized.tooltip: Also wait this long after the last input before snapping. Mostly for the mouse wheel, which moves the content directly and leaves NO velocity to decay — without a short quiet time the snap would fire between wheel notches and fight you.

src_serialized.name: flickMode
src_serialized.tooltip: Momentum = a flick travels its natural distance and the snap tidies up where it lands. Single Step = any flick above the threshold below advances exactly one step, however hard it was thrown.

src_serialized.name: flickVelocityThreshold
src_serialized.tooltip: How fast a release must be to count as a flick, in units per second. Only used in Single Step mode.

src_serialized.name: nextButton
src_serialized.tooltip: Optional. Drag a Button here and it moves one step forward — no code needed.

src_serialized.name: previousButton
src_serialized.tooltip: Optional. Drag a Button here and it moves one step back — no code needed.

src_serialized.name: stepMode
src_serialized.tooltip: Items = move a fixed number of items per press (Step Size). Page = move by however many WHOLE items currently fit in the viewport, so each press advances one screenful.

src_serialized.name: stepSize
src_serialized.tooltip: How many items one Next/Previous press moves, when Step Mode is Items. Ignored in Page mode.

src_serialized.name: wrapAround
src_serialized.tooltip: Wrap from the last item back to the first (and vice versa) instead of stopping at the ends.

src_members.name: OnSnapped
src_members.comment: Fires when a snap BEGINS, with the index being snapped to — not when the easing finishes. That is deliberate and depended upon: PaginationDots binds to it, and a dot that lit up only after the animation settled would feel broken.

src_members.sig: public int ItemCount => scrollRect != null && scrollRect.content != null ? scrollRect.content.childCount : 0
src_members.name: ItemCount
src_members.comment: For anything that wants to know the page count without reaching into the ScrollRect itself — e.g. Toolkit.UI.PaginationDots.BindToScrollSnap().

src_members.sig: public int CurrentIndex { get; private set; }
src_members.name: CurrentIndex
src_members.comment: WHICH ITEM YOU ARE ON. Updated live while you drag AND while the scroll is still coasting, so a "3 / 7" readout can simply read it each frame. For a one-off answer, call GetNearestItemIndex().

src_members.name: IsSettling
src_members.comment: True while the ScrollRect still owns the motion and the snap is waiting its turn. Useful if you want to grey something out until the list has settled.

src_members.name: OnBeginDrag
src_members.comment: Without this, grabbing the scroll again mid-snap would leave LateUpdate still forcibly animating toward the old target every frame, fighting the user's new drag input.

src_members.name: OnScroll
src_members.comment: The mouse wheel never snapped at all before, because the component only handled drags. Both this and the ScrollRect receive the event — the event system delivers to every handler on the GameObject — so this does not have to forward anything, and must not consume it.

src_members.sig: public static int FlickTargetIndex(int currentIndex, float velocity, int step)
src_members.name: FlickTargetIndex
src_members.comment: Which item a flick lands on. Positive velocity means the CONTENT is moving forward along the axis, which reveals EARLIER items — so it goes to the previous one.

src_members.sig: public static bool ShouldHandOff(float velocity, float secondsSinceInput, float speedThreshold, float quietTime)
src_members.name: ShouldHandOff
src_members.comment: The handoff rule, as one testable function: the motion has settled when it is slow enough AND the user has stopped feeding it input.

src_members.sig: public void SetStepMode(ScrollSnapStep mode, int itemsPerStep = 1)
src_members.name: SetStepMode
src_members.comment: Change how far a press travels at runtime — e.g. a "jump by page" toggle in an options menu. itemsPerStep is ignored in Page mode, where the viewport decides.

src_members.sig: public void SetFlickMode(ScrollSnapFlick mode) => flickMode = mode
src_members.name: SetFlickMode
src_members.comment: Swap the flick behaviour at runtime, so the two feels can be compared without re-entering Play mode.

src_members.name: CurrentStepSize
src_members.comment: How many items one press actually moves.  Page mode deliberately advances by a whole number of ITEMS that fit, not by exactly one viewport width: a viewport 2.6 items wide would otherwise land two thirds of the way through an item every press, which defeats the point of a snap. 2.6 items of room moves you 2.

src_members.name: ComputeCenteredNormalizedPosition
src_members.comment: Centres the chosen item in the VIEWPORT, as a normalized scroll position.  Returns a single float rather than a Vector2 on purpose: the old version returned a Vector2 whose OTHER component was 0, and LateUpdate then wrote both — so a horizontal snap also yanked a two-axis ScrollRect to the bottom of its vertical range on every release.

src_members.name: GetNearestItemIndex
src_members.comment: Finds the item whose centre is closest to the VIEWPORT's centre.
